question: Which country grows the great majority of the world's saffron?
answer: Iran. Estimates of its share run from about 80% to over 90% of a world harvest of a few hundred tonnes, much of it from Khorasan, where some fields are still watered by qanats, underground channels centuries old. Spain, whose name sells saffron at a premium, exports far more than it grows.
move: Ask where a product is grown, not where it was last packed.
trap: La Mancha labels are the famous ones, so Spain seems the source.
